newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Cold weather kills five more in Bucharest.
newsitem.headline: Cold weather kills five more in Bucharest.

text.p: Five homeless people have died in Bucharest in the past two days, bringing the death toll from a cold spell gripping Romania to 56 since Christmas eve, the city's morgue said on Wednesday.

"The five were found in stairwells or on the streets in the New Year and treated in hospital for severe pneumonia, but they didn't make it," Doctor Gheorghe Alexandrescu of the Bucharest Forensic Institute said by telephone.
He said 36 of the dead were homeless people who either froze to death or suffered from malnutrition combined with a variety of diseases.
Temperatures across Romania fell as low as minus 25 Celsius (minus 13 Fahrenheit) just after Christmas when blizzards blocked air, rail and road traffic for several days.
Temperatures have returned to normal since the New Year, but Bucharest residents must still cope with poor heating in their homes and snow piled high in uncleared streets.
The daily Libertatea on Wednesday said it had set up a "frost hot-line" to help people with badly heated homes.
